payload.text:
I'd hold off merging this branch. The tests pass, but the main promise in the README isn't met: every preview gets an ellipsis, even when nothing was cut. I ran the helpers on a few inputs; I didn't change anything.

**Must fix**
1. **Short text still gets "…".** In `src/excerpt.js`, `excerpt()` always cuts the text and adds "…". The README says text at or under the limit comes back unchanged and the ellipsis only appears when something was removed. When I ran it:
   - `excerpt('short', 50)` gave `"short…"`
   - `excerpt('', 5)` gave `"…"`, so an empty body shows a lone ellipsis.

   The function needs to return early when `trimmed.length <= limit`.
2. **It cuts one word too early when a word ends exactly at the limit.** `lastSpaceBefore` only checks the first `limit` characters, so it misses a space sitting right at the limit. `excerpt('one two three', 7)` gives `"one…"` instead of `"one two…"`, even though "one two" is exactly 7 characters. Checking `text[limit] === ' '` first, or looking at `slice(0, limit + 1)`, would fix it. The test in `words.test.js` currently asserts the wrong result (`3`) for this case.

**Should fix**
3. **The tests don't cover the cases above.** There's one test per file and none for "under the limit," an empty string or an exact boundary, so bugs 1 and 2 got through. I'd add those three tests.
4. **`toPlain` deletes underscores inside words.** `my_var_name` turns into `myvarname`, which matters for code-heavy snippets. It also leaves headings and list markers in place: `# Heading\n- item` becomes `# Heading - item`. The README says "markers removed," so either strip those too or narrow what the README claims.

**Worth knowing**
5. **Nothing uses the new helpers yet.** `src/card.js` didn't change on this branch, so cards still show the full body. If this branch was meant to add the preview under each card, that part is missing. If the wiring is coming in a later branch, it's fine as is.
6. **The "…" can go one character over the limit.** For example, a 15-character cut plus "…" is 16 characters. That's fine if `limit` means the text before the ellipsis; otherwise the README should say which it is.
7. **The changelog changes an old entry.** Besides adding 1.5.0, it rewords the existing 1.4.0 line ("a title and a body" becomes "a title and body"). That's harmless, but released entries usually aren't edited.

The version bump to 1.5.0 and the new changelog entry are otherwise fine.
